title.narrative: Provision of integrated WASH and Health high-impact interventions for vulnerable women and children in 7 Districts impacted by flash floods in Bangladesh

description.narrative: The proposed interventions aim to deliver urgent, high-impact, life-saving water, sanitation, hygiene (WASH), and health services to the most vulnerable communities affected by the floods in the targeted districts of Chattogram Division, including Feni, Noakhali, Cumilla, Laxmipur, Chittagong, Khagrachari (Hill Tracts), and Sylhet Division, including Moulvibazar. These efforts will ensure access to safe, sustainable, and climate-resilient WASH services, providing sufficient quantities of quality water for domestic use and access to safely managed sanitation services. The interventions will reduce the risk of life-threatening waterborne and sanitation-related diseases while upholding the dignity of vulnerable groups, particularly women and girls, and strengthening community resilience.Additionally, these interventions will support the health sector by delivering lifesaving medicines and emergency supplies to the affected population, particularly women and children, repairing damaged health facilities to immediately restore healthcare services, and ensuring the availability of adequate health staff to provide critical services in the affected areas. This will play a crucial role in saving the lives of women and children impacted by the devastating floods and improve their well-being and resilience, thereby reinforcing the humanitarian-development nexus. To maximize impact, WASH and health initiatives will be geographically aligned with other interventions in the CERF project areas.The activities will be implemented as follows:WASH (Target: 200,000 Beneficiaries)• Provision of water for drinking, cooking, and personal hygiene through the repair, construction, and disinfection of water points (deep tube wells with hand pumps, deep tube wells with submersible pumps, and other technologies).• Support for sanitation systems in emergency situations through the repair and construction of latrines to replace destroyed facilities, ensuring the safe containment of wastewater and minimizing spread of diseases.• Provision of essential WASH-related non-food items and supplies (e.g., water purification tablets, jerrycans, and hygiene kits) to reduce public health risks.• Hygiene promotion to raise awareness, ensuring active participation, and promoting accountability among affected populations in preventing and mitigating WASH-related diseases. This includes information/communication, promoting optimum use of facilities, and community mobilization and participation.Health (Target: 157,225 Beneficiaries)• Support Upazila health managers in preparing local level micro-plans for maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) service delivery in affected areas, ensuring the optimal use of available resources.• Create line list/database of pregnant women and children under one year of age, with a goal of ensuring at least 90 per cent receive quality MNCAH services.• Implement the Reaching Every Mother and Newborn (REMN) strategy to restore MNCH services, including antenatal care (ANC), postnatal care (PNC), safe delivery, expanded programme for immunization (EPI), and integrated management of childhood illnesses (IMCI) services.• Facilitate the referral of high-risk pregnant women and sick newborns with complications to higher-level healthcare centers.• Conduct minor renovations and provide logistical support, including essential lifesaving medicines and equipment, to selected primary healthcare (PHC) facilities to ensure they are equipped to deliver quality MNCAH services.• Engage local government representatives and religious leaders to identify vulnerable children and pregnant women, ensuring that lifesaving services reach those most in need.
